opex.name: Research and development

opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Up 17% YoY.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $140.89 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — while other income added $4.76 and tax cost $0.44, leaving a $36.57 loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $868,823K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $43.7M (a 5% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $355.3M, other income covered $41.3M of that and tax cost $3.8M, so the chart draws the remaining $317.8M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source.
oneTimers: $373.3M of stock-based compensation-related charges (including about $9.6M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions), excluded from non-GAAP results.
$23.9M of amortization of acquired intangibles, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
$1.8M of expenses associated with acquisitions and strategic investments, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $41.3M, net: $49.3M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, less $7.9M of other expense, net. Income tax was a $3.8M provision. Net loss attributable to Snowflake Inc. was $316.9M (EPS -$0.95), after $0.9M of loss attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 30% YoY and 95% of all revenue; product gross profit was $593.7M, a 72% margin.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Up 17% YoY — but it costs more to deliver than it brings in (a $12.9M gross loss).

sources.label: 10-Q for the quarter ended July 31, 2024 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 30% to $829.3M, the net revenue retention rate was 127%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already contracted — grew 48% to $5.2B. Snowflake guided Q3 FY25 product revenue to $850–$855M, up 22%, at a 3% non-GAAP operating margin.
takeaways.title: Product growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $355.3M, wider than the $285.4M loss a year ago. The main reason: $373.3M of stock-based compensation-related charges, including about $9.6M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions. Leaving those and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $43.7M, a 5% margin (down from 8% a year ago).
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay

takeaways.text: Snowflake ended the quarter with 510 customers spending over $1M a year on the platform (+28% YoY) and 736 Forbes Global 2000 customers (+5% YoY). Operating cash flow was $69.9M and adjusted free cash flow was $66.0M.
takeaways.title: Big customers kept spending

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 29% to $868.8M, with product revenue up 30% to $829.3M — but $373.3M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $355.3M and a net loss of $317.8M.
